sprint: Example Lifecycle, Backlog Backfill, and Reviewer Feedback Loop Hardening

questions.question: Does every planned example get a lifecycle record before generation?
questions.evidence: runner.py:584 iterates ctx.planning.ready_scenarios only. Blocked/excluded scenarios (ctx.planning.blocked_scenarios) are never registered in lifecycle_registry.
questions.gap: GAP-1: Excluded-by-allowlist scenarios get no lifecycle record.

questions.question: Does every generation failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: runner.py:596-599 calls mark_generation_failed() when example.status=='failed' or code is empty. runner.py:612-614 catches exceptions and marks generation_failed.

questions.question: Does every static validation failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: code_generator.py validates code (lines 72-85) but failures in validation are tracked as generation failure (status='failed'), not as a separate lifecycle stage. The lifecycle record exists but the failure_reason may conflate code-gen with validation.

questions.question: Does every build failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: runner.py:800-801 calls mark_build_failed() when validation result is not passed. runner.py:844-848 marks build failures as backlogged.

questions.question: Does every runtime failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: runner.py:810-811 calls mark_run_failed() with error text. runner.py:850-855 marks runtime failures as backlogged with medium priority.

questions.question: Does every output validation failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: Output validation failures are not tracked as a separate lifecycle stage. The lifecycle record has no mark_output_validation_failed() method. Output validation is bundled into the runtime stage.
questions.gap: Minor: output validation is implicit in runtime pass/fail.

questions.question: Does every reviewer failure get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: runner.py:921-926 calls mark_reviewer_failed() and mark_backlogged() when reviewer fails.

questions.question: Does every excluded-by-scope example get a lifecycle record?
questions.evidence: runner.py:584 iterates only ready_scenarios. Blocked scenarios from planner (blocked_pilot_not_in_scope) are never registered in lifecycle. This is the primary gap.
questions.gap: GAP-1: Critical. Excluded scenarios invisible to lifecycle system.

questions.question: Does every failed or excluded example get a backlog entry or taskcard?
questions.evidence: Failed examples (generation/build/runtime/reviewer) get backlog entries via runner.py:835-857. Excluded-by-allowlist examples have manual taskcards but no structured backlog entries. workspace/backlog/ directory does not exist.
questions.gap: GAP-2: No durable backlog for excluded scenarios.

questions.question: Does PR packaging list excluded examples and reasons?
questions.evidence: pr_builder.py has excluded_scenarios parameter (line 27) but publisher.py:214 and __main__.py:645 never pass it. PR body always shows 'None in this controlled pilot scope'.
questions.gap: GAP-3: PR body hides excluded scenarios.

questions.question: Does readiness rank count planned/generated/passed/failed/backlogged/packaged/excluded?
questions.evidence: family-generation-readiness-rank.json has controlled_pilot_pass_count and passing_types but lacks planned_count, excluded_count, backlogged_count, failed_count.

questions.question: Does the reviewer provide structured feedback that can drive regeneration?
questions.evidence: ReviewerResult in bridge.py has only available, passed, error, details fields. details is raw stdout (JSON or truncated string). No per-example structured findings (severity, file, line, symbol).
questions.gap: GAP-5: Reviewer feedback is pass/fail only.

questions.question: Does the repair loop actually consume reviewer feedback?
questions.evidence: Repair loop in runner.py:680-787 handles build and runtime repairs only. No reviewer repair loop exists. When reviewer fails, examples are just marked backlogged.

questions.question: Can the system learn from failures across runs?
questions.evidence: update_backlog_from_lifecycle() writes to persistent backlog JSON. But load_family_backlog() is never called before generation. Previous failure patterns are not fed into prompts.

questions.question: Can failed examples still disappear from latest evidence?
questions.evidence: Failed examples that get lifecycle records are preserved in example-lifecycle-records.json and backlog. But excluded-by-allowlist scenarios are NOT in lifecycle and can only be found in blocked-scenarios.json (which is promoted but not consumed by publisher/release-status). If a new run with different allowlist runs, previous blocked-scenarios.json is overwritten.
questions.gap: GAP-1 + GAP-2 combined: excluded scenarios can be lost.

scores.backlog_coverage: PARTIAL — works for generation/build/runtime/reviewer failures; missing for excluded-by-scope
scores.pr_summary_coverage: INCOMPLETE — excluded_scenarios parameter exists but unused
